transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Dr. Smith, my name is Belinda. I'm here today because I’ve started eating big amounts of food by myself at night, mostly because I’m just too embarrassed for anyone to see how much I’m actually eating.
After these episodes of eating large amounts of food, do you feel a need to engage in any behaviors to prevent weight gain, such as vomiting, using laxatives, or exercising excessively?

No, I don't do any of those things at all. I've never tried to make myself throw up, use laxatives, or do any kind of heavy exercising to make up for what I ate. I just sit there afterward with the heavy feeling and the guilt.
During these episodes, do you feel that your eating is out of your control, or do you feel like you could stop if you really wanted to?

It feels completely out of my control once I start, almost like a switch flips and I go on autopilot. I'll tell myself "you don't need this, Belinda, stop," but my hands just keep fixing another plate and I don't really decide when I'm done.
How many times per week, on average, do these episodes of eating large amounts of food occur, and how long has this been happening?

For the last five months, it's been happening about once or twice a week. It really started around the time my daughter and youngest grandbaby moved out of state and the house got so quiet in the evenings.
